fullPassage:
(A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

(B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

(C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!

✅ ④ academic emergency(학업 비상): 주 교육 규정상 '학업 비상' 상태에서 벗어나도록 하는 것이 목표라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: academic emergency = 학업 비상 상태. 주의 교육 규정(state's education rules) 하에서의 지위

questions.passage:
Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. (a) She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed.

That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at (b) her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one.

They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made (c) her want to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 매일 오후 소그룹 수업이 본문과 일치하는가
det.analysis:
✅ ① 매일 오후 소그룹 수업: 'every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level' — 본문 일치
❌ ② 처음부터 적극적: 학생은 'lacked patience and often lost focus' — 처음에는 부적극적
❌ ③ 학부모 상담: 본문에 학부모 언급 없음. 교사는 스스로 성찰(reflected)한 후 결정
❌ ④ 중학교 수학: 'elementary school(초등학교)'이며 읽기(reading) 지도
det.tip: every afternoon = 매일 오후. reading below grade level = 학년 수준 이하 독서

ch: 교사는 매일 오후 학년 수준 이하의 학생들과 소그룹 수업을 했다.
교사는 학부모와 상담 후 교육 방법을 바꿨다.

det.korean: 소그룹 수업 중단 여부 확인
det.analysis:
❌ ① 수준 맞는 책 선택: 'let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level' — 일치
❌ ② 방해 행동: 'she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself' — 일치
❌ ③ 번갈아 읽기: 'read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one. They would continue to swap back and forth' — 일치
✅ ④ 소그룹 중단: 본문에 소그룹 수업 중단 언급 없음. 오히려 학생이 소그룹에서도 향상('came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson')을 보였다
det.tip: 소그룹 수업 중단이 아닌, Emma가 소그룹에서도 더 잘 참여하게 된 것

ch: 교사는 학생의 수준에 맞는 책 중에서 고르게 했다.
학생은 집중력을 잃으면 주변을 방해하는 행동을 했다.
교사와 학생은 번갈아 가며 문단을 소리 내어 읽었다.
학생의 독서 능력이 향상되자 교사는 소그룹 수업을 중단했다.

questions.passage: Emma was a student who ①lacked patience. She often lost focus, at which point she ②became disruptive. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words. Sandy ③letting Emma select a book from a handful of books at ④her reading level.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① lacked=과거, ② became=과거, ③ let→letting 교체, ④ her=소유격
det.analysis:
❌ ① lacked: 'who lacked patience' — 과거시제 정상
❌ ② became: 'she became disruptive' — 과거시제 정상
✅ ③ letting: 원문은 'Sandy let Emma select'. let의 과거형은 let(불규칙동사 let-let-let). letting은 현재분사/동명사이므로 본동사로 부적절
❌ ④ her: 'at her reading level' — 소유격 her(Emma의) 적절
det.tip: let-let-let 불규칙 동사. 과거형도 let이다. letting은 현재분사/동명사

✅ ② 교사의 성찰과 개별 지도를 통한 학생의 독서 능력 향상: 교사가 성찰 후 일대일 지도를 시작하여 학생의 독서 능력과 자신감이 향상된 과정
❌ ③ 초등학교 교육 정책의 문제점: 정책 비판이 아닌 교사-학생 간 교육 성공 사례
❌ ④ 자기 주도 학습의 영향: 학생의 향상은 교사의 개별 지도 덕분이지 자기 주도가 아님
